question: Which of the following carbon compounds shows the presence of a branched chain structure?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Butane (C4H10)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Butane (C4H10)** is an **alkane** with **four carbon atoms**. It is the first hydrocarbon in the series that can form a **branched chain structure** known as **isobutane** (or **2-methylpropane**), where one carbon atom is attached to the center carbon of a three-carbon chain. ***Hence, option 1 is correct.***
 
• **Ethane (C2H6)** consists of **two carbon atoms** connected by a single bond. Because it only has two carbons, they can only be arranged in a **straight line**, making branching impossible. ***Hence, option 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Cyclohexane (C6H12)** is a **cycloalkane** where **six carbon atoms** are joined in a **closed-ring structure**. While it contains multiple carbons, its primary arrangement is **cyclic** rather than a branched open chain. ***Hence, option 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Methane (CH4)** is the simplest **hydrocarbon**, containing only **one carbon atom** bonded to four hydrogen atoms. Since there is only one carbon, there is no possibility of any **chain formation** or branching. ***Hence, option 4 is incorrect.***
 
• In organic chemistry, **branching** occurs when at least one carbon atom is bonded to **three or four** other carbon atoms, a phenomenon that requires a minimum of **four carbon atoms** in an open-chain alkane.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Structural Isomerism:**
 
 
• This is a form of **isomerism** where compounds have the same **molecular formula** but different **structural arrangements** of atoms.
 
• **Butane** has two structural isomers: **n-Butane** (straight chain) and **isobutane** (branched chain).
 
• As the number of **carbon atoms** increases, the number of possible **isomers** increases significantly. For example, **Pentane (C5H12)** has **three** isomers, while **Hexane (C6H14)** has **five**.
 
 
 
• **Hydrocarbon Classification:**
 
 
• **Alkanes:** Saturated hydrocarbons with the general formula **CnH2n+2**. They contain only **single covalent bonds**.
 
• **Alkenes and Alkynes:** Unsaturated hydrocarbons containing **double** or **triple bonds**, respectively.
 
• **Cycloalkanes:** Saturated hydrocarbons where the carbon atoms are arranged in a **ring**, following the formula **CnH2n**.
 
 
 
• **Physical Properties of Branched Chains:**
 
 
• **Branching** generally lowers the **boiling point** of a compound compared to its straight-chain isomer.
 
• This is because a **branched-chain** molecule has a more **spherical shape**, which reduces the **surface area** and weakens the **Van der Waals forces** between molecules.
 
• For instance, **n-butane** has a boiling point of approximately **-0.5 degrees Celsius**, while **isobutane** boils at **-11.7 degrees Celsius**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Carbon's Tetravalency:** Carbon has **four valence electrons**, allowing it to form **four covalent bonds**. This property, known as **tetravalency**, combined with **catenation** (the ability to link with other carbon atoms), allows the formation of complex **straight, branched, and cyclic** structures.
 
• **Nomenclature:** According to **IUPAC** rules, the branched isomer of butane is named **2-methylpropane** because the longest continuous chain has **three carbons** (propane) and a **methyl group** is attached to the **second carbon**.
 
• **Natural Occurrence:** **Butane** is a highly flammable, colorless gas that is easily **liquefied**. It is commonly used as a fuel in **LPG (Liquefied Petroleum Gas)** cylinders and **cigarette lighters**.
